sections.html:
Lakewood is the most populous city in Jefferson County and the fifth largest in Colorado, immediately west of Denver. The 2020 census counted 155,984 residents. Ground rules differ by area: a house near Belmar, one near Green Mountain and one along West Colfax may have little in common beyond the city name. A good offer starts with the specific address.

Government is the biggest employment group, led by the Denver Federal Center. A job tied to a federal or state agency can come with a transfer order and a firm report date, and a seller on that clock cares most about certainty of closing. If your house sits near a W Line light rail station, say so, since transit access draws a particular set of buyers.

Older neighborhoods developed before the city incorporated, when water, fire protection and services came district by district. Some lacked street lights and sidewalks, and a buyer of an older Lakewood house may ask about lighting, sidewalks and utilities.

Small creeks and gulches cross the city and drain east toward the South Platte, among them Lakewood Gulch, Weir Gulch, Sanderson Gulch and Bear Creek. Lakes and reservoirs dot the map too. If your property sits next to a gulch or reservoir, a buyer's inspector may look closely at grading and basement moisture.

  • Note any past water in a basement or crawl space and what was done about it.
  • Keep records of gutter, grading or sump work.
  • Tell a buyer about known issues up front instead of leaving them for the inspection.

Lakewood requires a license to operate a short-term rental, and the City Clerk's Office handles applications. Online applications for new licenses opened May 1, 2023, and incomplete applications are not accepted.

The clerk's office is at 480 S. Allison Parkway. For licensing, write to STR@lakewoodco.gov or call 303-987-7080. The city also runs an online complaint form for unlicensed rentals.

If you own a house you rented short term and want out, a cash sale means you do not need to find a buyer who wants the license.

PaymentDue date
First installmentFebruary 28, or the next business day
Second installmentJune 15
Full paymentApril 30

Colorado collects taxes in arrears, so each bill covers the prior year. Jefferson County sends one notice, by the end of January. Delinquent notices follow in July, and a tax lien sale takes place each November for unpaid real property. When a due date falls on a Friday or a weekend, the county accepts payment the next business day without interest.

Lakewood owners pay the Jefferson County Treasurer in Golden. The office is at 100 Jefferson County Parkway, Suite 2520, open Monday through Thursday and closed on Fridays.

If a balance is open, ask the treasurer for the amount and give it to your title company. The title company shows it on the closing statement and pays it from your proceeds. Because the tax lien sale happens each November, an old unpaid year deserves attention well before it reaches that point.

Belmar is the town center, mixing retail, residential, cultural and public space, and the Lakewood Cultural Center houses a theater, gallery space and art classrooms. Heritage Lakewood Belmar Park holds historic buildings near Kountze Lake. When a buyer asks about the neighborhood, those are fair points to mention.

sections.h2: How a Lakewood cash sale works
sections.html:
A cash sale skips the lender, so closing depends on title work and your preferred date. We buy as-is, so you leave out the repairs and staging a listing usually demands.

That fits several common situations: an inherited house, a house with tenants, a rental you want to exit before licensing becomes a burden, or a fixed move date. Send us the address and your timeline, and we respond with an offer or an honest explanation.

After you accept an offer, a title company searches the records, confirms who owns the house and orders the tax certificate. It prepares the deed, you sign, and the deed is recorded. The company then pays off any taxes and loan balance and sends you what remains. If the property has tenants, share the lease early so the buyer can plan. If the house served as a short-term rental, tell the buyer and ask the clerk's office how its license is treated on a sale.

Gather the latest tax notice, your mortgage servicer's number and any repair records before you start. A complete folder shortens the title work and gets you to the signing table sooner.

Heirs with a house they do not want, landlords leaving the rental business, owners with a transfer and a report date, and anyone facing a repair bill they would rather skip all make up the typical caller. Request an offer, compare it with a listing after repairs, fees and waiting, and pick the better fit for your schedule. You may find that the extra months of ownership cost more than the difference in price.

sections.h2: Selling a Lakewood house with tenants
sections.html:
Tenants do not have to leave before you sell. Share the lease, the rent and the move-out plans, and the buyer will price the situation. Some buyers want the tenants to stay and keep collecting rent, others want a vacant house. Tell the buyer which you prefer. If the unit is already empty, say how long it has been empty and whether anything inside has deteriorated.

Deferred repairs are common on rentals, and they are the main reason owners choose an as-is sale. You avoid scheduling contractors around a tenant's calendar.

sections.h2: What gets priced into an offer
sections.html: Roof, heating and cooling, plumbing, electrical, foundation and finishes all matter, along with anything unusual about the lot, such as a gulch behind the house. A buyer who closes with cash prices those items directly, so you will not see a second round of negotiation after an inspection report arrives. Basement moisture history, if you have any, belongs in the first conversation. So do roof age, the last time the furnace was serviced, and any permits you pulled for past work. Honest answers keep the number steady from the first quote to the final closing statement.

sections.h2: Allow time for the title work
sections.html: Closing speed depends largely on the title company. A clean ownership record and a tax balance you already know move fast. A missing signature from an heir, an old lien or an unclear estate slows things down. If any of those apply, mention them early so they can be worked on while the rest of the paperwork proceeds.

faqs.q: What county is Lakewood, CO in?
faqs.a: Jefferson County, where it is the most populous city. Property tax goes to the Jefferson County Treasurer in Golden.

faqs.q: When are property taxes due in Lakewood?
faqs.a: The first installment is due February 28 or the next business day, the second June 15, and a single full payment April 30. Taxes are collected in arrears, so the bill covers the previous year.

faqs.q: When does Jefferson County hold its tax lien sale?
faqs.a: Each November, for unpaid real property. Delinquent notices go out in July, so clear any old balance before then.

faqs.q: Do I need a license to rent my Lakewood house short term?
faqs.a: Yes. The City Clerk's Office handles the short-term rental license, and online applications for new licenses opened May 1, 2023. Check the current ordinance for the full requirements.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Lakewood house as-is for cash?
faqs.a: Yes. We buy houses in their present condition, so you do not need to repair or clean the property before closing.
